recommendations: Benchmark launch prices against ThePetNest, the closest match (same marketplace model, already live in Ludhiana): dog Rs 899 / 1,199 / 1,599, cat Rs 899 / 1,999. PetDoorStep's S full groom (Rs 1,199) is at parity, but L (Rs 1,899) is above ThePetNest's top tier. Either include dematting and de-shedding in L or set it at Rs 1,599-1,699. Keep Bath & Brush at Rs 599-899 as the entry and acquisition product.

Model commission on grooming at 15-20% at launch, rising to 20-25% once supply is dense. Urban Company's beauty precedent is 8.5-25% (average about 20-22%). Do not copy Urban Company's 34-36% consolidated 'take rate', which includes customer fees and product sales.

Use a capped, slab-based commission like Urban Company's appliance 'SLA' plan: a small fixed fee per job (e.g. Rs 50-100) plus a slab commission capped at about Rs 300-400. Capping the fee on high-ticket jobs (spa, large dogs) cuts the incentive to go direct; research shows commissions roughly double off-platform deals and leakage rises with job price.

Because customers pay the provider in cash or UPI after service, collect commission through a prepaid provider credit wallet. Require a minimum balance (e.g. Rs 500) to receive bookings and deduct each job's commission automatically, as Urban Company does with its 50-credit minimum and auto top-up. This avoids chasing dues and needs no payment-gateway build at launch (confirm RBI aspects with a CA or lawyer).

Keep any provider 'Pro' plan optional, cheap (Rs 299-499/month, well under the roughly Rs 1,600/month an average Justdial advertiser pays) and value-based: priority bookings, a lower commission slab, discounted kits. Avoid upfront deposits tied to job targets; Urban Company's Rs 2,000-3,000 minimum-guarantee plan led to protests and a lawsuit, and its appliance unit dropped subscriptions.

Do not offer minimum guaranteed earnings. Urban Company's InstaHelp-style Rs 20-25k/month guarantees are VC-funded and loss-making (about Rs 381 lost per order). Recruit groomers on take-home economics instead: at Rs 1,199-1,599 a groom and 15-20% commission, 25-30 grooms a month nets roughly Rs 25-35k. That is competitive with Urban Company's Rs 28,322 average.

Add a low-capex ancillary line by selling grooming consumables (shampoo, tick/flea products, blades, towels) and starter kits to providers at a margin. Urban Company made Rs 187-188 crore (about 16% of revenue) this way in FY25. Keep purchases optional.

Design 'Groom Club' as a prepaid bundle, not a pure discount fee. Indian pet and home-service memberships cost only Rs 250-500 a year for 10-15% off (UC Plus, Zigly Pro, ThePetNest Premium) or are free (HUFT Rewards). For example, sell 6 baths + 2 full grooms a year paid upfront at 10-15% off. Prepayment locks in repeat bookings on-platform and improves cash flow.

Re-price walking. Sploot charges Rs 2,400 (20 min) and Rs 3,540 (40 min) a month in Chandigarh, and local walkers expect about Rs 3,000-4,000 per dog per month. Rs 2,999 less a 20% commission underpays walkers. Use a 10% commission on walking or set Rs 2,999 for 30 minutes and Rs 3,499-3,999 for 45 minutes, with walk length stated.

Keep the vet home visit at Rs 699 (matches Supertails' Rs 699 visit plus consult) and the vaccination visit at Rs 199 + MRP, which undercuts Supertails' Rs 799 home rabies bundle. Run a sensitivity case at Rs 499: Vetic shows funded chains can drop home visits to Rs 199-299 if they enter Punjab. Expect vet GMV to ramp slowly, since Supertails' vet services were only Rs 2.65 crore of Rs 108 crore revenue.

Build cheap anti-leakage measures from day one: masked calling via a low-cost cloud telephony provider; benefits that apply only on-platform (re-groom or injury guarantee, membership pricing, loyalty points); a 'rebook my groomer' feature like ThePetNest's, so customers don't need the groomer's number; customer reporting of offline offers; and a published warn-then-block policy modelled on Urban Company's.

Plan for HUFT store-plus-spas in Ludhiana, Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula and Amritsar as the main organised rival. HUFT offers Rs 500 off the first spa visit, so budget a Rs 200-300 first-booking discount in customer acquisition cost and position on doorstep convenience and no travel stress for the pet.

List PetDoorStep on Justdial's free listing and Google Business Profile for demand. Avoid paid Justdial packages with ECS auto-renewal and a 3-month notice period until unit economics are proven. Recruit providers from independent Tricity and Ludhiana groomers (Monika's, Pet Vanity, Justdial groomers), who already charge Rs 1,000-1,900 and resent paying for unqualified leads.

recommendations: Set grooming commission at 20-25% (provider keeps 75-80%). Urban Company runs at about 28% and beauty partners protested at 30%. On a Rs 1,499 medium full groom the groomer keeps about Rs 1,125-1,200, minus about Rs 60-150 of consumables and Rs 20-40 of fuel. At 2 grooms a day for 24 days that is about Rs 45,000-50,000 a month net, well above salaried Punjab groomers (Rs 15,000-35,000). Recruit by pitching 'double your salon salary'.

For walking, price Rs 2,999 a month at Rs 100 per walk and take only 10-15% (walker keeps about Rs 85-90 per walk). A 25% cut leaves Rs 75, below metro norms of Rs 70-200. Alternatively raise the walking price to Rs 3,499, or charge walkers a flat Pro plan instead of a percentage.

For vets, aim to pay about Rs 500-550 of the Rs 699 visit fee (a 20-25% take) and let the vet keep any drug or vaccine margin. Target fresh GADVASU BVSc graduates and Ludhiana private-clinic vets for evening or weekend slots. A fresher earning Rs 20,000-35,000 needs about 40-60 visits a month to match a salary.

Do not use para-vets for any vaccination, deworming or consult visits. Route every medical service through a vet registered with the Punjab Veterinary Council until a lawyer confirms the s.30 position. Groomers can do baths, haircuts, nail and ear cleaning only.

Asset-light kit: providers own their kits. Specify a minimum kit of about Rs 18,000-19,000 (Codos CP-9700, 3800W IndiaMART dryer, scissor set, foldable tub, budget 5L shampoo; table optional). Negotiate a bulk price with an IndiaMART or Delhi wholesaler and offer kit-on-EMI recovered from weekly payouts, as Urban Company did with kit loans, rather than buying kits yourself. A pro kit costs about Rs 85,000-1,10,000 and is only for top groomers.

For verification, the low-cost path is PP Saanjh employee verification (Rs 200, up to 30 days) plus an Aadhaar QR check through the Aadhaar app (free) or a vendor (about Rs 10): about Rs 250 per provider. The standard path adds a SpringVerify or JantaKhoj court/address package at Rs 800-1,600 plus GST. Start Saanjh applications at least 30 days before launch.

Charge providers a one-time onboarding fee of Rs 249-499, as ThePetNest does. This covers verification (about Rs 250) plus uniform and ID (about Rs 400-550: two Ludhiana-made logo polos at Rs 185-215 and a PVC card with lanyard), so supply onboarding costs the platform close to nothing.

Skip Rs 49,000-65,000 academy courses. Recruit groomers with 1+ year of salon experience and run a 3-5 day in-house onboarding (handling, hygiene and app SOPs, two supervised grooms) led by one senior groomer paid per session.

Budget travel at Rs 2-2.5 per km in fuel (petrol Rs 105.8 a litre). Cluster bookings by zone, keep the free radius to about 8 km, and add a Rs 50-100 travel surcharge beyond it, passed to the provider. Revisit if fuel prices rise further.

Model a contingent social-security levy of 1-2% of platform turnover (capped at 5% of provider payouts) from the date the government notifies it, and register providers on the government portal within 45 days of onboarding.

recommendations: Treat every number in this R3 output as provisional (UNVERIFIED, no web access this run), and have a CA confirm the 5-6 rows that drive the model (s.9(5) applicability, the grooming GST rate, TCS/194-O mechanics, entity choice, aggregator levy) before finalising. Day 1 at zero cost: Udyam registration on the government portal (not paid look-alike sites), a grievance officer and provider details on the website (E-Commerce Rules 2020), a privacy notice and consent checkbox (DPDP), and PMSBY enrolment (Rs 20/year) as a condition of provider onboarding.

Entity, low-cost path: start as a sole proprietorship, or an LLP if a liability shield is wanted. An LLP needs no audit until Rs 40 lakh turnover and costs about Rs 500 in government fees plus professional fees. Standard path: a Pvt Ltd via SPICe+ (zero MCA fee up to Rs 15 lakh capital, but a mandatory audit every year), and only if raising external equity within about 18 months. Apply for DPIIT recognition (free) once incorporated as an LLP or Pvt Ltd.

Keep the platform clearly an agent, not the supplier: the provider is named as the service supplier on the customer bill or bill of supply, PetDoorStep issues a separate commission invoice to the provider, and T&Cs say the provider is an independent supplier free to accept or decline jobs. Book only commission plus subscriptions as net platform revenue and treat GMV as a memo line.

In the model, keep provider GMV GST-free while individual providers stay under Rs 20 lakh a year (Notification 65/2017). Switch on 18% GST on commission and subscriptions from the month the platform's own turnover is projected to cross Rs 20 lakh in a FY, which is certain before reaching Rs 1 crore of cumulative net revenue. Show net revenue ex-GST.

Add a downside scenario in which s.9(5) 'housekeeping' is applied to grooming (18% GST on grooming GMV, paid by the platform), and stress-test whether the take rate survives it. Do not launch with pricing that only works if this risk is zero.

Keep customer payments flowing directly to providers (UPI/cash) at launch. This avoids GST TCS (s.52) registration and RBI payment-aggregator issues. Still budget for s.194-O TDS at 0.1% of GMV for providers above Rs 5 lakh a year (recover it via commission invoices), plus a TAN and quarterly 26Q filing (CA fee). If central collection is added later, use an authorised PA's split-settlement product.

Model a contingent aggregator social-security levy of 1-2% of platform turnover (capped at 5% of provider payouts) from FY 2026-27, until the central notification clarifies rate and base. Also add Punjab State Development Tax of Rs 2,400/year for the founder.

File a trademark in Class 44 (grooming and veterinary) at Rs 4,500 using Udyam or DPIIT status. Add Classes 45 and 35 at Rs 4,500 each when cash allows, so total government fees are Rs 13,500 for three classes.

Vet vertical: onboard only vets with Punjab State Veterinary Council / VCI registration. The vet procures and bills vaccines and medicines at MRP under their own practice, and PetDoorStep takes commission only on the visit fee, never holding drug stock.

Do not count pet-insurance referral income in the model until a licensed IRDAI partner or POSP arrangement exists. Get 2-3 quotes for CGL with a care, custody and control (animal bailee) extension before launch, since premiums could not be sourced this run.

recommendations: Size the serviceable market bottom-up, not from national reports. Ludhiana MC has about 45,880 car-owning households (SECC; likely 60-80k today). Assuming 15-25% have a dog gives about 7,000-20,000 target dog households. At 23.7% groomer usage, the core paying pool is about 1,700-4,700 households. Rs 1 crore cumulative GMV at about Rs 1,400 average ticket needs about 7,100 bookings, or about 450-600 active grooming customers at 6-8 grooms a year over 24 months. That is roughly 10-30% of the core pool, so plan Tricity expansion before claiming the Rs 1 cr target from Ludhiana alone.

Model customer frequency explicitly. Use 6 grooms a year for long or double-coated breeds and 3-4 for short coats, a 35-45% first-to-second booking rate in year 1, rising toward 60%+ for Groom Club members. Do not use the 80-95% repeat claims from Supertails or BhaoBhao as base case.

Paid CAC assumption: Rs 500-800 base (low case Rs 300, high case Rs 1,200), derived from Meta home-services CPL of Rs 100-250 and 25-40% lead-to-booking conversion, plus 18% GST on ad spend if not GST-registered. Budget Rs 15,000-25,000 a month of Meta spend for months 1-3 (Rs 500-800/day) and expect Q4 (Oct-Dec) CPMs 25-50% higher, so keep launch-month spend lean.

Make Click-to-WhatsApp ads on Instagram Reels the primary paid channel: Reels CPM is the cheapest placement at Rs 45-140, and a CTWA click opens a free messaging window of up to 7 days. Target a 3-5 km radius around affluent wards rather than city-wide.

WhatsApp stack, low-cost path: the free WhatsApp Business app until about 250-500 customers (256-recipient broadcast lists). Then AiSensy Basic at Rs 1,350/month (annual) + GST. Budget utility reminders at Rs 0.115 + GST each. Since 1 Oct 2026 service replies also cost Rs 0.115 beyond any free allowance, so 1,000 customers getting 3 reminders a month cost about Rs 400/month. Use marketing templates (Rs 0.8631 + GST + BSP markup, about Rs 1.0-1.3 each) sparingly.

Google: create a Google Business Profile on day 1 and push every completed job to leave a review (free). Hold Google Search ads until you can spend at least Rs 15,000 a month; below that, agencies say there is too little data to optimise.

Justdial: start with the free listing. Buy a paid package (about Rs 18,000-36,500 a year) only after 2-3 months of tracking enquiry quality, and negotiate quarterly terms. Standard-case annual line item: Rs 0 (low-cost) vs Rs 20,000-36,500 (standard).

Offline launch kit, low-cost version (about Rs 12,000-20,000): 5,000 A5 flyers with a QR code linking to WhatsApp (Rs 2,500-10,000), inserted into newspapers on routes in target sectors (about Rs 1,000-1,750 per 5,000 at Rs 0.20-0.35 each), plus 3-5 roll-up standees (Rs 950-1,800 each) placed at partner vet clinics and pet shops in exchange for referral commission. Book a stall or demo at the GADVASU Dog Show in December 2026.

Influencers: avoid cash micro-influencer deals (Rs 5,000-25,000 per Reel). Run barter with 5-10 Ludhiana and Chandigarh nano pet creators: a free full groom (Rs 1,199-1,899 value) for a disclosed Reel plus a unique referral code. Track per-creator barter value under Rs 20,000 a year to stay below the 194R TDS threshold, and require #ad/#collab disclosure.

Referral programme: double-sided Rs 150 credit to the referrer and Rs 150 off the friend's first groom, released only after the friend's first completed and paid booking. This is slightly richer than Urban Company's Rs 100/100 because of the higher ticket. Assume 3-5% of active customers refer each month and referrals supply 10-20% of new customers by month 6 (assumption).

Make the vaccination visit (Rs 199 + vaccine) and anti-rabies awareness a low-CAC entry product. Ludhiana's very high dog-bite incidence (28,390 district cases in 2024) makes vaccination messaging resonate, and it seeds the customer list for grooming upsells.

open_questions: Exact NPCI circular text: does the 0.4% UPI MDR (from 15 Oct 2026) apply to gateway/PA-routed online collections the same way as QR, and how is an individual provider receiving on a personal VPA classified (P2P vs P2PM)?

Chandigarh Angels Network and Ludhiana Angels Network typical cheque sizes and next cohort dates.
INR prices of .in domains at Indian registrars, and official Zoho Bookings / Zoho FSM INR pricing (only reseller figures found).
Status of the Stand-Up India relaunch and of the Budget 2025 Rs 2 crore first-time entrepreneur (women/SC/ST) loan scheme.
needs_CA_or_lawyer: Under RBI PA Directions 2025, can PetDoorStep collect customer payments into its own account and then pay providers (Razorpay's suggested 'two-step' flow) without PA authorisation, or must it use Route/Easy Split only? What payer-payee transparency documentation is needed?

If customers pay providers directly (provider's UPI QR or cash) and PetDoorStep bills providers for commission, does Section 194-O TDS (0.1%) still apply, given it can apply to payments made directly by the buyer? Is the Rs 5 lakh individual-participant exemption usable?

Does GST TCS under Section 52 (0.5%) apply when the platform does not collect the consideration? Must PetDoorStep register for GST compulsorily as an e-commerce operator (Sec 24) even below Rs 20 lakh turnover?

GST treatment of PetDoorStep's commission and 'Groom Club'/'Pro' subscriptions (18%?), and whether veterinary home-visit services by registered vets are GST-exempt health-care services for animals, which would affect the vet-visit commission structure.
Can individual groomers and walkers onboarded via the platform stay unregistered under Notification 65/2017 (aggregate turnover up to Rs 20 lakh)?

Does UPI MDR (0.4% above Rs 2,000) hit walking packages (Rs 2,999/4,999) and Spa services collected into a P2M merchant account? Since MDR cannot be passed to customers, which entity should be the payee?

Entity choice (proprietorship vs LLP vs Pvt Ltd) and incorporation timing to preserve SISFS (<2 years old at application), DPIIT/80-IAC, CIIF NIDHI-SSP (company required) and MUDRA/CGTMSE eligibility.
Equity, convertible or debt terms from incubators (CIIF NIDHI-SSP, VLIIF) and angel networks (LAN Rs 50 lakh equity): valuation, dilution, exit clauses.
Eligibility of an asset-light service marketplace for PMEGP (eligible project cost, EDP training) and for the Punjab IBDP 8% interest subsidy on a MUDRA loan.
recommendations: Payments Phase 1 (until about Rs 40 lakh annual turnover): don't collect customer money centrally. Customers pay each provider directly to the provider's own free UPI QR or in cash, after service, as already planned. As individual small merchants under Rs 1 lakh a month, providers should stay at zero MDR (P2PM). PetDoorStep then bills each provider weekly for commission through a UPI QR or payment link. This avoids the 2% + GST gateway fee (about Rs 2.36 lakh on Rs 1 crore GMV) and Razorpay Route's Rs 40 lakh turnover gate. Have a CA confirm the 194-O and TCS position first.

Control commission leakage in Phase 1 with a refundable provider security deposit or prepaid commission wallet (e.g. Rs 2,000-5,000). Use booking IDs logged in Google Sheets/AppSheet and a weekly reconciliation, and suspend providers who don't settle within 7 days.

Phase 2 (after crossing about Rs 40 lakh turnover, or for prepaid Groom Club subscriptions): move to Razorpay Route or Cashfree Easy Split. Model about 2.36% (PG + GST) plus about 0.3% (transfer fee + GST) of collected GMV, and time Razorpay activation so the 0% offer (90 days / Rs 5 lakh) covers launch. If not using Route, batch provider payouts weekly via RazorpayX at Rs 4-6 + GST each (about Rs 850 a month for 30 providers).

Model UPI MDR from 15 Oct 2026 as 0.4% only on tickets above Rs 2,000 collected into a P2M (non-small) merchant account: walking Rs 2,999 costs Rs 12 and Rs 4,999 costs Rs 20. Grooms of Rs 2,000 or less cost nothing. Do not plan to pass MDR to customers; NPCI forbids it.

Low-cost ops stack for the first 6-12 months, about Rs 500-1,000 a month: free WhatsApp Business app; one Google Workspace Business Starter seat at about Rs 319 with GST, which should include AppSheet Core (verify) to build the booking board and provider job app on Sheets; Google Forms or Jotform free for provider onboarding; Cloudflare Pages free site; .in domain at about Rs 1,000 a year. Standard-cost alternative: Zoho One at about Rs 1,250-1,500 per employee per month plus GST, or Glide Business at about $199-249 a month.

Defer a custom app until booking volume justifies it, roughly 500+ bookings a month or 30+ active providers. Standard cost: agency Rs 20-55 lakh. Low-cost: Indian freelancer or consultant Flutter + Supabase MVP at Rs 6.5-10 lakh, Android-only first ($25 Play fee, skip Apple's Rs 8,700 a year). Avoid clone scripts for anything beyond a demo.

Move from the WhatsApp Business app to the API (BSP at about Rs 1,000-2,500 a month plus about Rs 0.115 per utility message) only when automated reminders or confirmations are needed. Use utility templates for booking confirmations and reminders and keep marketing templates (about Rs 0.86 each) to a minimum.

Funding route, cheapest first: (1) Register with Startup Punjab and DPIIT (free). (2) Apply to GADVASU's VLIIF incubator, the best domain fit: veterinary network, up to Rs 10 lakh ignition grant, link to Ludhiana Angels Network. Incubation also unlocks the Punjab seed grant (Rs 3-5 lakh via incubators) and the 25% lease-rent reimbursement. (3) Consider CIIF Chitkara NIDHI-SSP (Rs 10-25 lakh, equity or debt) after 3 months of association. (4) Pitch LAN's next Fuelerator cohort (Rs 50 lakh equity) only once traction exists.

Debt for working capital and provider kits: a MUDRA Kishore loan (up to Rs 5 lakh, collateral-free, no SBI processing fee, about 9-12% interest). Pair it with the Punjab IBDP 8% interest subsidy if eligible, which could make net cost about 2-4% (verify). Don't build the base model on PMEGP (status after March 2026 unconfirmed, poor fit for asset-light) or Stand-Up India (ended March 2025; women/SC/ST only).

Incorporate as a Private Limited company (or LLP) before applying to incubators or SISFS, but time it so the company is under 2 years old when an SISFS application is likely. Budget CA fees for incorporation and GST advice in the investment sheet.
Skip soundboxes (PhonePe Rs 125 a month or Rs 999 + Rs 25 a month). Doorstep providers can show a free static QR on their phone or a printed card; the provider app or WhatsApp confirms payment.

facts.claim: In Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026), Urban Company's India Consumer Services revenue was Rs 356 crore on NTV of Rs 1,056 crore, an implied take rate of about 33.7%. DSIJ's own calculation gives the same 33.7%.
facts.source_name: DSIJ App Mindshare; Kotak Neo Q1 FY27 results coverage
facts.notes: Derived ratio. Urban Company does not disclose a take rate. It bundles customer convenience/platform fees with partner commissions, so it is NOT a commission-only benchmark. Consolidated Q1 FY27 was NTV Rs 1,465 cr and revenue Rs 528 cr (~36%), per https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/urban-company-q1-fy-2026-27-results-revenue-up-shares-jump-despite-loss/. Figures come from search-result extracts because page fetching was blocked in this environment.

facts.topic: Urban Company take rate trend (analyst consensus)
facts.claim: S&P Global consensus has Urban Company's core India Consumer Services take rate rising from 30.6% in 2023 to about 36% in 2026. Take rates for the InstaHelp quick-househelp service are expected to stay at 22-23%.
facts.source_name: S&P Global Market Intelligence
facts.notes: These are analyst estimates, not company disclosure. They show a mature category leader taking about 30% early and moving toward 36% only after years of density. A new entrant in a Tier-2 city should model lower.

facts.claim: Commissions and fees took 28.3% of Urban Company service professionals' average gross earnings in 9M FY26. Inc42 says this is not the company's overall take rate. Urban Company also charges customers a convenience fee, earns consumer membership fees, and sells tools and consumables to professionals. It does not split convenience fees from commissions.
facts.source_name: Inc42, 'Inside Urban Company's Marketplace Model'
facts.notes: Published in 2026 (it cites 9M FY26 data). This is the best available proxy for what a mature Indian home-services marketplace deducts from the provider side.

facts.claim: After an Oct 2021 protest, Urban Company cut its maximum beauty-category commission from 30% to 25%. It said commissions ran from 8.5% on small orders to 25% on high-ticket orders, with an average of about 20-22%. It also capped monthly penalties per partner at Rs 1,500.
facts.source_name: Urban Company blog; Free Press Journal / Moneylife coverage
facts.notes: Official source but dated, so current slabs may differ. Grooming at home is most similar to UC's salon-at-home, so a 20-25% commission is the closest Indian precedent. Protesters in 2021 alleged rates up to 30-35%.

facts.topic: Urban Company hybrid lead-fee + slab commission (appliance repair)
facts.claim: Under Urban Company's 'SLA' commission structure for appliance partners, each job costs a fixed lead credit of Rs 120 (12 credits). A post-job commission is then debited by job value: Rs 0 for jobs up to Rs 250, Rs 30 for Rs 251-500, Rs 65-130 for Rs 501-1,000, Rs 150-225 for Rs 1,001-1,500, Rs 240-320 for Rs 1,501-2,000, Rs 340-399 for Rs 2,001-2,350, and a flat Rs 399 above Rs 2,350. The earlier subscription plan was removed and 'no initial investment' is required.
facts.value: Rs 120 lead fee + Rs 0-399 slab commission per job
facts.source_name: Urban Company partner support helpsite (PX Appliances)
facts.notes: Internal agent-facing page; date and currency not confirmed. Worked examples: a Rs 1,200 job pays Rs 120 + Rs 180 = Rs 300 (25%), and a Rs 199 visit pays Rs 120 (60%). The total is capped at Rs 519, which is 22% of a Rs 2,350 job and falls further on bigger tickets. This is a useful template for a capped commission that lowers the incentive to leak high-ticket jobs.

facts.topic: Urban Company prepaid partner credit wallet
facts.claim: Urban Company partners receive job leads only while their credit balance is at least 50 credits. On payout day the system automatically deducts from payouts to top the balance back up (shown as 'Reconciliation Recharge' / 'System transfer to credit balance'). Commission is deducted from online payouts, and cash-paid orders sit in a separate app section.
facts.source_name: Urban Company partner support helpsite (PX EPC/Pest)
facts.notes: Two internal articles give different thresholds (50 vs 200). At Rs 10 per credit (inferred from 12 credits = Rs 120), 50 credits is about Rs 500. This is the mechanism a pay-after-service, cash/UPI-to-provider model needs to collect commission upfront.

facts.claim: In Dec 2021 Urban Company introduced a 'minimum guarantee plan'. Beauty partners paid Rs 3,000 (Salon Prime) or Rs 2,000 (Salon Classic) upfront for guaranteed leads, against a target of at least 40 jobs a month. Partners protested, and Urban Company sued four of the protesters.
facts.source_name: The Wire; The Quint; Inc42
facts.notes: Sources disagree on whether the deposit was forfeited or refundable if the target was missed. Urban Company's appliance vertical later dropped its subscription for per-job fees (R1-05). Takeaway: an upfront provider 'Pro' fee tied to targets is contentious.

facts.claim: In 9M FY26, Urban Company's active service partners averaged Rs 28,322 a month in net earnings in hand, up from Rs 26,489 a year earlier. The top 20% averaged Rs 42,418, the top 10% Rs 47,471 and the top 5% Rs 51,673.
facts.source_name: Urban Company Investor Relations (Earnings Index 9M FY26)
facts.notes: Net of commissions and costs, metro-weighted. The release headline says Rs 28,332 while the body says Rs 28,322. This is the benchmark for what a full-time provider expects. Ludhiana groomers will likely compare PetDoorStep take-home with roughly Rs 20-30k/month.

facts.topic: Ancillary revenue: selling kits/consumables to providers
facts.claim: Urban Company earned about Rs 187-188 crore in FY25 from selling tools and consumables (beauty kits, repair tools, cleaning gear) to service professionals. That is roughly 16% of its Rs 1,144.5 crore operating revenue, up about 27% year on year. Some gig workers say they are pressured to buy through the platform.
facts.source_name: The Captable; Entrackr; MediaNama
facts.notes: The 16% share is my calculation. It points to a low-capex extra revenue line for PetDoorStep: margin on shampoos, tick/flea products and grooming kits sold to providers. Keep purchases optional to avoid the coercion criticism.

facts.topic: Minimum guaranteed earnings schemes (instant home help)
facts.claim: Urban Company's InstaHelp reportedly gives workers an assured income of about Rs 20,000-25,000 a month at Rs 150-180 an hour. Rival Pronto promises Rs 22,000-30,000, and Snabbit charges customers about Rs 169-199 an hour. InstaHelp was estimated to lose about Rs 381 per order.
facts.source_name: The Week
facts.notes: Guaranteed-income models need venture funding (InstaHelp posted an EBITDA loss of Rs 131.6 cr in Q1 FY27). They are not viable for a bootstrapped marketplace. They do raise provider expectations in metros.

facts.topic: Customer membership norm: Urban Company Plus
facts.claim: Urban Company Plus membership gives 15% off every service plus priority booking. Coupon sites list it at Rs 299 for 6 months or Rs 399 for 12 months, while a student teardown cites Rs 249 for 6 months. The plan is location-specific, and early cancellation is generally not refunded.
facts.source_name: Zoutons coupon aggregator; NextLeap teardown
facts.notes: No official UC page was seen and prices conflict. This sets the Indian norm: memberships are cheap (under Rs 70/month) and discount-led, so a 'Groom Club' fee cannot be a major revenue line on its own.

facts.claim: Supertails' FY25 operating revenue was Rs 108.3 crore (up 68%) with losses of about Rs 52.5 crore. facts.topic: Disintermediation - how Urban Company polices it
facts.claim: Urban Company's partner FAQ defines offline booking as a partner taking requests directly from a customer by call or SMS, for example after collecting the customer's number on a first job. Customers report it in the app, and Urban Company verifies before acting. Partners get warnings via the app or WhatsApp and can be blocked until they complete training. Another version calls it 'Zero Tolerance', with removal from the platform.
facts.source_name: Urban Company partner support helpsite; JM Financial report (Feb 2026); RHP summaries
facts.notes: A JM Financial note (Feb 2026, bsmedia.business-standard.com) has a section 'Disintermediation Risk Persistent But Interventions Rolled-out'. Motilal Oswal calls it a structural risk in repeat, trust-based categories. Urban Company's RHP lists 'platform circumvention risk'. Pet grooming and walking are exactly such repeat, trust-based categories.

facts.topic: Disintermediation evidence - home cleaning platform study
facts.claim: A Kellogg/SSRN study of a Moscow home-cleaning app, which marked up cleaner fees by up to 40%, used high-frequency geolocation and found no evidence of cleaners returning to client homes off-platform. It estimates that no more than 1 in 83 relationships formed on the app end in disintermediation.
facts.source_name: Astashkina, Bray, Momot, Salikhov - SSRN / Kellogg
facts.notes: An academic working paper from a single platform. It suggests leakage is often overestimated when the platform adds real value (scheduling, payments, trust).

facts.claim: A study of an on-demand cargo-delivery platform (Lalamove) found that introducing a commission raised leakage by nearly 4 percentage points, doubling detected off-platform transactions. Leakage was more likely on higher-priced jobs, and customers typically received about half of the commission savings. Counterfactuals suggest non-fulfilment penalties plus distance-based commission discounts reduce leakage.
facts.source_name: Xie & Zhu, 'Platform Leakage' (PKU HSBC Business School seminar abstract)
facts.notes: Implication: higher or uncapped commissions on high-ticket jobs (spa, large-dog groom, monthly walking) drive leakage. Use capped or declining commission (as in R1-05) and keep the walking commission low.

facts.topic: Legal - Indian Veterinary Council Act 1984 s.30
facts.claim: Section 30 bars anyone other than a registered veterinary practitioner from holding a veterinary post or practising veterinary medicine in a state. A proviso lets a state government, by order, permit diploma or certificate holders (veterinary supervisors, stockmen, stock assistants) to render 'minor veterinary services' only under the supervision of a registered veterinary practitioner. Each state must notify its own list of minor services.
facts.value: Only RVPs may practise; para-vets only under RVP supervision
facts.source_name: India Code - IVC Act 1984; Indian Kanoon (https://future.indiankanoon.org/doc/137091); DFID minor vet services report
facts.notes: Statute text was seen via search extracts, not a full read. Practical effect: vaccination, deworming and vet consults should be done by vets registered with the Punjab Veterinary Council (or the VCI register). Para-vets cannot run independent pet home visits. Lawyer to confirm.

facts.topic: Legal - Punjab minor veterinary services notification
facts.claim: Punjab notified its minor veterinary services list on 2 Nov 2006 (Dept of Animal Husbandry) and repeated it on 17 May 2011. The list includes securing animals, drenching, injections, castration of farm ruminants and vaccination, all under a registered practitioner's supervision.
facts.value: Vaccination by para-vets only under RVP supervision
facts.source_name: NDDB Dairy Knowledge Portal - Punjab notification compilation
facts.notes: The list is livestock-oriented. A 2006 Tribune report cites an earlier 1998 Punjab letter. Whether a para-vet may vaccinate pets at a customer's home under remote supervision is unclear; needs a lawyer.

facts.topic: Legal - Punjab HC on s.30 supervision
facts.claim: In CWP-23149-2018 (Punjab State Veterinary Officers Association), decided 29 Apr 2026, the Punjab & Haryana High Court pressed the state to implement s.30. The state said it had placed Veterinary Inspectors under Veterinary Officer supervision. The court called one VO supervising 9-10 dispensaries unworkable. The state reported 969 of 1,508 sanctioned VO posts filled.
facts.source_name: Punjab & Haryana High Court judgment copy (third-party hosted)
facts.notes: Courts read s.30 supervision as requiring real, functional supervision. A model where para-vets do pet visits under nominal vet supervision is legally risky.

A vendor (eKYCNow / Message Central) charges Rs 10 per offline verification with no setup fee. UIDAI's online authentication fees (Rs 20 per e-KYC in 2019, cut to Rs 3 in 2021) apply only to licensed AUA/KUA entities and were revised again by Circular 15 of 2025 (8 Dec 2025).

facts.notes: The new rupee amounts in Circular 15 were not visible. UIDAI's new Aadhaar app (2025) supports QR and face-auth sharing. A PTI report (Nov 2025) says UIDAI may discourage offline verification by some entities. A startup should not store Aadhaar numbers.

facts.topic: Legal - gig worker social security (aggregator levy)
facts.claim: The Code on Social Security 2020 came into force on 21 Nov 2025. Aggregators must contribute 1-2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of amounts paid or payable to gig and platform workers. The Seventh Schedule covers e-marketplaces for goods or services, professional services providers, healthcare and 'any other goods/services platform'. The Social Security (Central) Rules 2026 were notified around 8-9 May 2026 and require worker registration on the government portal within 45 days. The contribution start date and rate await a separate notification.
facts.source_name: Taxmann; IMPRI (https://www.impriindia.com/?p=75715); ThePeoplesBoard (https://www.thepeoplesboard.com/?p=18176)
facts.notes: A doorstep pet-services marketplace likely falls under 'professional services provider' or 'any other' platform. Model it as a contingent cost of 1-2% of net platform revenue once notified. Lawyer or CA to confirm.

facts.claim: A supplier of services must register for GST once aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds Rs 20 lakh. The Rs 10 lakh threshold applies only to the special-category states (Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura), and Punjab is a normal-category state. Aggregate turnover is counted per PAN across India and includes exempt supplies such as veterinary services.
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of CGST Act 2017 s.22(1) and s.2(6), as amended by the CGST (Amendment) Act 2018
facts.notes: No web access in this run: the WebSearch budget was used up and every WebFetch/curl failed (DNS/egress blocked). The URL is the official CBIC GST portal root and was NOT opened. The fact is well established but should be verified. If the agent model holds, the platform's own turnover is its commission plus subscriptions, not GMV.

facts.topic: GST compulsory registration - ECO and suppliers via ECO
facts.claim: Under s.24(x) CGST, an e-commerce operator that must collect TCS under s.52 has to register regardless of turnover. Notification 65/2017-Central Tax exempts persons supplying SERVICES through an ECO from compulsory registration under s.24(ix) while their aggregate turnover stays within the s.22 threshold (Rs 20 lakh in Punjab).
facts.value: Providers via the platform need no GST registration below Rs 20 lakh; an ECO collecting payments must register from day 1
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of CGST Act s.24(ix)/(x) and Notification 65/2017-Central Tax dated 15-11-2017
facts.notes: Not fetched (web blocked). This drives the design decision: if customers pay providers directly by UPI/cash and the platform collects no consideration, s.52 TCS does not apply. In that case s.24(x) arguably does not force registration until the platform's own turnover crosses Rs 20 lakh. A CA must confirm.

facts.claim: An ECO that collects consideration on behalf of suppliers must collect TCS on the net value of taxable supplies. From 10 July 2024 the rate is 0.25% CGST + 0.25% SGST (0.5% intra-state, 0.5% IGST inter-state); it was 1% before. Notification 15/2024-Central Tax made the change. The ECO files GSTR-8 monthly.
facts.value: 0.5% of net taxable supplies (0.25% CGST + 0.25% SGST)
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of CGST Act s.52 and Notification 15/2024-Central Tax dated 10-07-2024 (53rd GST Council)
facts.notes: Not fetched. TCS applies only where the ECO collects the consideration and only on taxable supplies, so exempt vet services are excluded. In practice it cannot be credited for unregistered suppliers. If the platform collects payments, it must register (s.24(x)), file GSTR-8 by the 10th, and withhold 0.5% from provider payouts.

facts.topic: GST s.9(5) - services where the ECO pays the tax
facts.claim: Notification 17/2017-Central Tax (Rate), as amended, lists the services on which the ECO itself pays GST under s.9(5). They are passenger transport (radio taxi, motorcab, maxicab, motorcycle), accommodation services, restaurant services (from 1 Jan 2022), and 'housekeeping services such as plumbing, carpentering etc.' except where the supplier is itself liable to register under s.22(1). Pet grooming, walking and vet services are not named.
facts.value: Pet care is not expressly notified; 'housekeeping' wording is open-ended
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Notification 17/2017-CT(Rate) dated 28-06-2017, housekeeping entry inserted by Notification 23/2017-CT(Rate) dated 22-08-2017
facts.notes: Not fetched. This is a high-impact risk. If a tax officer treated at-home grooming as 'housekeeping', the platform would owe 18% GST on the full grooming GMV supplied by unregistered groomers, about 15% of the GST-inclusive price, which would wipe out the commission margin. The model should carry a downside scenario until a CA or an AAR ruling confirms it does not apply.

facts.topic: GST rate on platform commission / subscriptions
facts.claim: Commission or service fees charged by a marketplace to service providers, and customer membership fees such as 'Groom Club', are standard-rated at 18% GST (intermediary/support services, SAC 9985/9983 family). Providers that are not registered cannot claim this input tax credit back.
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Notification 11/2017-CT(Rate), residual 18% entry (unchanged in the Sept-2025 rate rationalisation)
facts.notes: Not fetched. Once the platform is registered, 18% on commission is a real cost to unregistered groomers. Model net platform revenue EXCLUDING GST and decide whether commission rates are quoted GST-inclusive or GST-exclusive. The exact SAC code is for a CA to confirm.

facts.claim: Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) exempts (Nil rate) 'services by a veterinary clinic in relation to health care of animals or birds' (Heading 9983, believed to be Sr. No. 47).
facts.value: Nil GST on vet consultation fee
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Notification 12/2017-CT(Rate) dated 28-06-2017
facts.notes: Not fetched. The entry says 'veterinary clinic', so whether a registered vet's home visit qualifies needs a CA view, though home visits are generally treated as covered. Medicines or vaccines sold at MRP are a separate supply of goods (or possibly a composite supply). The platform's commission on vet bookings is still 18%. Exempt turnover counts toward the provider's Rs 20 lakh aggregate turnover.

facts.topic: GST rate on pet grooming / walking
facts.claim: Pet grooming and dog walking have no specific GST entry and default to the 18% residual rate. The GST rate rationalisation effective 22 Sept 2025 cut 'beauty and physical well-being' services (salons, barbers, gyms, yoga) to 5% without ITC, but those entries cover human services and probably do not extend to animal grooming.
facts.value: 18% (if the supplier is registered); nil if the supplier is unregistered and under Rs 20 lakh
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of the 56th GST Council decisions (3 Sept 2025), effective 22-09-2025
facts.notes: Not fetched. Most individual groomers will stay under Rs 20 lakh and unregistered, so their customer prices carry no GST. A groomer (or a platform treated as principal) that registers would charge 18%. Classification needs CA confirmation.

facts.claim: A platform taxes only its commission/fee if it acts as an ECO or intermediary and the independent provider is the legal supplier. If instead the platform sets fixed prices, sells under its own brand, invoices the customer in its own name, guarantees the service, and controls and pays the providers, tax authorities may treat it as the principal supplier. GST (once registered) and income tax would then fall on the full GMV.
facts.value: Commission-only taxable base vs full-GMV base
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - analysis based on CGST Act s.2(44)/(45) (e-commerce/ECO), IGST Act s.2(13) (intermediary), CGST Rules r.33 (pure agent)
facts.notes: Not fetched; this is analysis, not a cited ruling. The decided model (fixed published price list, 'PetDoorStep' brand, vetting, post-service payment) has several principal-like features. Mitigations: provider-supplier T&Cs, a bill of supply/invoice in the provider's name issued 'on behalf of', a separate commission invoice to the provider, provider freedom to accept or decline jobs. The same question decides whether accounts book GMV or net revenue (AS 9 / Ind AS 115).

facts.topic: Income tax TDS by ECO - s.194-O
facts.claim: An e-commerce operator must deduct TDS on the gross amount of services facilitated through its platform. The rate fell from 1% to 0.1% from 1 Oct 2024 (Finance (No.2) Act 2024). Payments a customer makes directly to the provider are deemed paid by the ECO and are included. No TDS is needed for an individual/HUF participant whose gross amount for the FY is Rs 5 lakh or less and who has furnished PAN/Aadhaar.
facts.value: 0.1% of gross; Rs 5 lakh exemption per individual provider
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Income-tax Act 1961 s.194-O, as amended by Finance (No.2) Act 2024
facts.notes: Not fetched. The deeming rule means the platform owes TDS even when customers pay the groomer directly in cash or UPI. It then has to recover the 0.1% through the commission settlement, which needs a TAN and quarterly 26Q returns. A full-time groomer at about Rs 1 lakh GMV a month (Rs 12 lakh a year) crosses Rs 5 lakh. Where 194-O applies, 194C/194J do not.

facts.claim: The Income-tax Act, 2025 (assent August 2025) replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026 (tax year 2026-27). Its TDS provisions, including the ECO TDS equivalent of s.194-O, sit in a consolidated tabular section (s.393). Rates and thresholds were broadly carried over.
facts.value: Effective 1 April 2026; TDS consolidated in s.393
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Income-tax Act 2025
facts.notes: Not fetched. The exact table entry and serial number for ECO TDS under s.393, and any rate change, must be confirmed. The 'previous year/assessment year' concept became a 'tax year'.

facts.claim: If the platform itself pays providers rather than the 194-O route applying: s.194J TDS on professional fees (e.g. vets) is 10%, and the per-payee annual threshold rose from Rs 30,000 to Rs 50,000 from 1 April 2025. s.194C TDS on contract work is 1% for individuals/HUF and 2% for others, with thresholds of Rs 30,000 per payment and Rs 1,00,000 aggregate per FY.
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Income-tax Act 1961 s.194J/194C as amended by Finance Act 2025
facts.notes: Not fetched. These apply only if PetDoorStep pays providers as contractors or professionals, which is the principal model. In a true marketplace, 194-O at 0.1% displaces them.

facts.topic: Presumptive taxation (founder as proprietor; individual providers)
facts.claim: Under s.44AD (business), profit is deemed at 8% of turnover, or 6% for digital receipts, for resident individuals/HUF/partnership firms (not LLPs or companies) with turnover up to Rs 2 crore (Rs 3 crore if cash receipts are 5% or less). Under s.44ADA (specified professions), profit is deemed at 50% of receipts up to Rs 50 lakh (Rs 75 lakh if cash is 5% or less). Under the new regime, the s.87A rebate makes total income up to Rs 12 lakh tax-free from FY 2025-26.
facts.value: 44AD 6-8% deemed profit; 44ADA 50%; nil tax up to Rs 12 lakh income
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of s.44AD/44ADA (Finance Act 2023 limits) and s.87A (Finance Act 2025)
facts.notes: Not fetched. This matters for the founder only if trading as a sole proprietor, and lets most groomers and walkers pay little or no income tax. Whether vets fall under 44ADA 'medical profession' is for a CA to confirm.

facts.claim: A private limited company opting for s.115BAA pays 22% + 10% surcharge + 4% cess = 25.168% effective, but cannot claim s.80-IAC. The regular regime is 25% + cess for turnover up to Rs 400 crore. An LLP pays a flat 30% + 4% cess (31.2%), plus a 12% surcharge above Rs 1 crore income.
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Income-tax Act / Finance Act rate schedules
facts.notes: Not fetched. A bootstrapped marketplace will likely make losses in its early years, so the rate difference matters less than compliance cost and fundraisability.

facts.claim: An eligible startup (a company or LLP, incorporated on or after 1 April 2016 and before 1 April 2030, turnover up to Rs 100 crore, holding an Inter-Ministerial Board certificate in addition to DPIIT recognition) can deduct 100% of profits for any 3 consecutive years out of its first 10. Finance Act 2025 extended the incorporation window to 2030.
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Income-tax Act s.80-IAC as amended by Finance Act 2025
facts.notes: Not fetched. Sole proprietorships are not eligible, and IMB approval rates are low. Little practical value until the business makes profits, and it is not available to a company that has opted for 115BAA.

facts.claim: DPIIT recognition is free and online. It is open to private limited companies, LLPs and registered partnership firms (not sole proprietorships) up to 10 years from incorporation, with turnover up to Rs 100 crore in any FY, that work on innovation or a scalable model. Benefits include self-certification under 6 labour and 3 environmental laws, IPR fee rebates and fast-tracking, eligibility for the 80-IAC application, and Fund of Funds/SISFS access.
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of DPIIT notification G.S.R. 127(E) dated 19-02-2019 (startup definition)
facts.notes: Not fetched. The turnover and age limits may have been revised after 2019 (possible upward revision in 2025-26), so verify. Recognition also unlocks the startup trademark fee rate (Rs 4,500).

facts.claim: Udyam registration is free, Aadhaar/PAN-based and self-declared on the official Udyam portal. From 1 April 2025 a micro enterprise is one with investment up to Rs 2.5 crore and turnover up to Rs 10 crore. Benefits include MSME delayed-payment protection, CGTMSE collateral-free credit and the reduced trademark fee.
facts.value: Rs 0 fee; micro limit Rs 2.5 cr investment / Rs 10 cr turnover
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of MSMED Act s.7 classification as revised (Budget 2025, effective 01-04-2025)
facts.notes: Not fetched. Paid third-party 'Udyam' sites exist, but the government portal is free. A sole proprietor can register too, so this is the cheapest day-1 registration.

facts.topic: Private limited company - government fees & annual compliance
facts.claim: Incorporating via MCA SPICe+ has a zero filing fee for authorised capital up to Rs 15 lakh. Name reservation is about Rs 1,000, plus state stamp duty on MoA/AoA and DSCs for directors. Annual duties: statutory audit for every company regardless of turnover, AOC-4 and MGT-7/7A filings, ADT-1 auditor appointment, director KYC, and an INC-20A commencement declaration within 180 days.
facts.value: Rs 0 MCA filing fee (<=Rs 15 lakh capital) + ~Rs 1,000 name + stamp duty + DSC
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules 2014 as amended
facts.notes: Not fetched. Punjab stamp duty, DSC cost, and professional fees (Vakilsearch/IndiaFilings/ClearTax packages) plus annual CA/CS fees could not be sourced in this run; see open_questions. The mandatory audit makes a Pvt Ltd the costliest entity to run each year.

facts.claim: The LLP incorporation fee scales with contribution (Rs 500 for contribution up to Rs 1 lakh). Each year it files Form 11 (annual return, due 30 May) and Form 8 (statement of accounts and solvency, due 30 Oct). An audit is needed only if turnover exceeds Rs 40 lakh or contribution exceeds Rs 25 lakh. Late filing costs Rs 100 per day per form.
facts.value: Rs 500 registration fee (contribution <= Rs 1 lakh); no audit below Rs 40 lakh turnover
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of LLP Act 2008 s.34-35 and LLP Rules 2009 (Annexure A fees, r.24(8))
facts.notes: Not fetched. A cheaper annual-compliance alternative to a Pvt Ltd that still qualifies for DPIIT, but investors usually require conversion to a Pvt Ltd before equity rounds. Professional fees are not sourced.

facts.claim: Under the Trade Marks Rules 2017, the TM-A application fee is Rs 4,500 per class (e-filing) for individuals, startups (DPIIT) and small enterprises (Udyam), versus Rs 9,000 per class for others (Rs 5,000/10,000 for physical filing). Relevant Nice classes: 44 (animal grooming, veterinary services), 45 (pet sitting/dog walking), 35 (online marketplace), and 9/42 (app/software).
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Trade Marks Rules 2017, First Schedule
facts.notes: Not fetched. The usual timeline is examination in a few months, then a 4-month opposition window after journal publication, with unopposed marks typically registered in about 8-18 months. Registration lasts 10 years, and TM can be used from filing. Filing Class 44 alone costs Rs 4,500; filing 44+45+35 costs Rs 13,500.

facts.topic: Punjab professional tax (Punjab State Development Tax)
facts.claim: The Punjab State Development Tax Act 2018 levies Rs 200 per month (Rs 2,400 per year) on persons engaged in professions, trades, callings and employment who are assessable to income tax. Employers deduct it from salaried employees whose income is taxable.
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of the Punjab State Development Tax Act 2018
facts.notes: Not fetched. The founder pays it if income-tax assessable, and it would also apply to any future salaried staff above the taxable limit. Whether an entity (LLP/company) also pays, and the enrolment procedure, are for a CA.

facts.claim: The rules apply to marketplace e-commerce entities offering goods OR services. Obligations: appoint a grievance officer and show their name and contact on the platform; acknowledge complaints within 48 hours and resolve them within one month; display seller/provider details (name, address, contact, ratings), the price breakup, and refund/cancellation and payment terms; avoid manipulating prices or posting fake reviews; and levy no cancellation charges unless the entity bears similar charges itself. The CCPA Dark Patterns Guidelines (30 Nov 2023) also ban 13 dark patterns.
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 (notified 23-07-2020) and Dark Patterns Guidelines 2023
facts.notes: Not fetched. Compliance costs almost nothing (website pages, a grievance email or WhatsApp, a provider details card) and is needed from launch.

facts.claim: The DPDP Rules 2025 were notified in November 2025 with a phased start. Data Protection Board provisions applied at once, consent-manager provisions after about 12 months, and most data-fiduciary duties (notice, consent, security safeguards, breach notification to the Board and affected users, erasure, grievance handling, verifiable parental consent for children) after about 18 months (around May 2027). Maximum penalties reach Rs 250 crore for failing to maintain security safeguards.
facts.value: Core obligations from ~May 2027; max penalty Rs 250 crore
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of the DPDP Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025 (notified Nov 2025)
facts.notes: Not fetched, so the exact notification date and phase dates need verifying. There is no blanket small-business exemption. A low-cost path: a privacy notice, consent checkbox, data minimisation (address, phone, pet details), access controls on provider apps, and a breach SOP.

facts.topic: Code on Social Security 2020 - aggregator contribution
facts.claim: The four labour codes, including the Code on Social Security 2020, came into force on 21 Nov 2025. Under s.114(4), aggregators (Schedule VII lists categories including e-marketplace and professional services provider) contribute 1-2% of annual turnover to a gig/platform worker social security fund, capped at 5% of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers. The rate and scheme are fixed by central government notification.
facts.value: 1-2% of turnover, capped at 5% of payouts to workers
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of the Code on Social Security 2020 s.114 and Schedule VII; commencement 21-11-2025
facts.notes: Not fetched. Whether the contribution rate, fund, aggregator registration (e-Shram) and any turnover threshold had been notified by Oct 2026 is unconfirmed. Whether 'turnover' means GMV or the platform's own revenue is critical for the model. As a prudent placeholder, provision 1-2% of net platform revenue, capped at 5% of provider payouts.

facts.claim: Rajasthan enacted the Platform Based Gig Workers (Registration and Welfare) Act 2023 with a welfare cess on aggregators, and Karnataka enacted a platform-based gig workers social security and welfare law in 2025 with a welfare fee on payouts. No Punjab gig-worker law is known to the model.
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of state legislation
facts.notes: Not fetched. Whether Punjab or Chandigarh UT has passed or proposed a gig-worker law by Oct 2026 remains open. Expansion beyond Punjab is only to other Punjab cities and the Tricity (Chandigarh UT and Haryana's Panchkula).

facts.claim: The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Pet Shop) Rules 2018 require registration with the State Animal Welfare Board for establishments that sell or trade pet animals. The Dog Breeding and Marketing Rules 2017 cover breeders. Neither expressly covers at-home grooming, walking or vet visits where no animals are sold, though the general cruelty offences in PCA Act 1960 s.11 apply to anyone handling animals.
facts.value: Likely not applicable to an at-home grooming platform
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of the PCA Act 1960 and PCA (Pet Shop) Rules 2018
facts.notes: Not fetched. These rules would apply if PetDoorStep later sells animals or runs boarding or daycare premises. Grooming SOPs (no sedation by non-vets, restraint limits, heat safety) reduce cruelty and liability risk.

facts.claim: Indian Veterinary Council Act 1984 s.30 says only a registered veterinary practitioner (on a State or the Indian Veterinary Practitioners Register) may practise veterinary medicine. Diploma or certificate holders may give minor veterinary services only under supervision.
facts.value: Vets on the platform must be registered with Punjab State Veterinary Council / VCI
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of the Indian Veterinary Council Act 1984 s.30
facts.notes: Not fetched. Vaccinations and tick/deworming treatments involving prescription drugs should be given by or under a registered vet. Collect each vet's registration number at onboarding and display it.

facts.claim: Retail sale or stocking of drugs, including veterinary drugs and vaccines, needs a drug sale licence under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 and Drugs Rules 1945. Registered practitioners supplying medicines to their own patients fall under a limited exemption. Selling above MRP breaches Legal Metrology rules.
facts.value: Platform should not itself stock or sell medicines without a licence
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 / Rules 1945
facts.notes: Not fetched. Safer model: the vet buys, carries and bills medicines and vaccines under their own practice or a tie-up chemist, and PetDoorStep's commission excludes medicine value. A lawyer must confirm how the vet-dispensing exemption applies to veterinary practitioners.

facts.claim: Insurance Act 1938 s.40 bars paying commission or remuneration for soliciting or procuring insurance business to anyone other than a licensed insurance agent or intermediary. Earning pet-insurance referral fees therefore needs an IRDAI licence (e.g. corporate agent, insurance marketing firm, or a POSP tie-up) or an arrangement through a licensed broker or web aggregator.
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Insurance Act 1938 s.40/s.42 and IRDAI intermediary regulations
facts.notes: Not fetched. Keep pet-insurance referral revenue out of the model until a licensed partner structure (and its revenue share) is confirmed.

facts.claim: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana provides Rs 2 lakh accidental death or total disability cover (Rs 1 lakh for partial disability) for ages 18-70 at Rs 20 per year (raised from Rs 12 from 1 June 2022), auto-debited from a bank account.

facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of the PMSBY scheme (premium revision effective 01-06-2022)
facts.notes: Not fetched. This is a low-cost alternative to a commercial Group Personal Accident policy: require or help each provider to enrol at onboarding. It does not cover third-party or pet-injury liability.

facts.topic: Payment collection - RBI payment aggregator rules
facts.claim: Under RBI rules on payment aggregators (Guidelines of 17 March 2020, as updated), an entity that receives customer funds on behalf of merchants and settles them on is doing payment aggregation, which needs RBI authorisation. Marketplaces typically avoid this by using an authorised PA's split-settlement or route product, so funds never pass through the platform's own account.
facts.value: Use an RBI-authorised PA split/route product if collecting customer payments
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of RBI Guidelines on Regulation of Payment Aggregators and Payment Gateways (17-03-2020)
facts.notes: Not fetched. Collecting all GMV into the founder's or company's own UPI account and paying groomers later creates PA, TCS (s.52) and principal-characterisation risk at once. The decided pay-provider-directly model avoids this but makes commission recovery harder.

facts.claim: GST e-invoicing (IRN) is mandatory only for registered persons whose aggregate turnover exceeded Rs 5 crore in any FY from 2017-18 (from 1 Aug 2023, Notification 10/2023-Central Tax).
facts.source_name: UNVERIFIED THIS RUN - model knowledge of Notification 10/2023-Central Tax dated 10-05-2023

facts.claim: Census 2011 counted Ludhiana city at 1,618,879 people (2001: 1,398,467). Ludhiana district had 3,498,739, of which 2,069,708 were urban and 1,429,031 rural.

facts.topic: Stray dog density / dog bites Ludhiana
facts.claim: Ludhiana district recorded 28,390 dog-bite cases in 2024, the highest in Punjab; 13,488 were in the city. The MC says about 1.5 lakh stray dogs have been sterilised since 2015.
facts.source_name: The Tribune (Ludhiana)
facts.notes: Relevant to the walking service: stray encounters are an operational and liability risk. It also supports demand for anti-rabies vaccination visits. Tribune e-paper reports put city cases near 13.7k for 2025.

facts.source_name: The Tribune (Punjab)
facts.notes: Preliminary figures. District-level and breed-wise pet-dog tables were not found. The 20th census (2019) Ludhiana stray-dog table exists on Indiastat (paywalled). A 2022 Vet Sci study estimated a median of 672,005 stray dogs in Punjab (95% CI 241,802-1,198,024).

facts.claim: About 32 million Indian households had pets in 2024, up from about 26 million in 2019 (Redseer via Entrepreneur India). Euromonitor puts India's total pet population at about 39 million in 2025, growing about 5% a year.
facts.source_name: Entrepreneur India citing Redseer; Euromonitor via GII report summary

facts.source_name: Redseer Strategy Consultants
facts.notes: Metro-skewed sample, likely 2024. Another undated source cites about Rs 4,000/month with 75-80% on food. Supports a Groom Club price well below Rs 1,000/month.

facts.topic: India pet services / pet care market
facts.claim: India's pet services market (grooming, boarding, daycare, training) was about USD 485 million in 2023 and is expected to pass USD 1 billion by 2030 (>11% CAGR). Total pet-care estimates range from USD 884M (Ken Research, 2025) to USD 3.6B (2024, cited by India Briefing).

Other URLs: https://www.kenresearch.com/industry-reports/india-pet-care-market and https://www.india-briefing.com/news/indias-pet-care-economy-2025-an-overview-37234.html

facts.claim: In a TGM Research India survey, 23.7% of pet owners use groomer services and 22% use pet training.
facts.source_name: TGM Research - Pet care survey India
facts.notes: Survey sample and date not verified. Penetration in Tier-2 cities is likely lower. Use it as an upper bound on the share of dog households that would book paid grooming.

facts.claim: Indian vet chain Vetic recommends professional grooming every 4-8 weeks and nail trims every 4-6 weeks. A vet blog says a professional groom every 1-3 months is enough for most dogs that are brushed at home.
facts.source_name: Vetic blog; VetHelpDirect
facts.notes: Implies 6.5-13 professional grooms a year in theory. For modelling, assume 4-8 a year for long or double coats and 2-4 for short coats, since Indian owners often bathe at home. Coat-type guidance: long-haired 4-6 weeks, short-haired 6-10 weeks.

facts.claim: BhaoBhao, a Mumbai at-home dog and cat grooming startup founded in 2025, reports more than 3,000 clients, a 95% repeat rate, repeat customers booking monthly, and prices of Rs 1,500-2,000 per visit. It raised USD 200K from angels.
facts.source_name: StartupWired; Entrepreneur India
facts.notes: The repeat claim is unverified and its definition is unclear. The price point is a metro (Mumbai) benchmark, about 25% above PetDoorStep's medium-dog full groom. Supertails also self-reports an 80% repeat rate (undated, Entrepreneur India).

facts.claim: Grooming-business benchmarks: 60-70% of clients return for at least a second appointment within 12 months, 30-40% of first-time clients book a second appointment, typical gap between visits is 4-8 weeks, and the target rebooking-at-checkout rate is 60% or more.
facts.source_name: Dojo Business (salon retention guide); Franpos

Second source: https://franpos.com/dog-grooming-marketing-ideas (60% rebook target). Suggested model ramp: month-1 repeat 35-45%, rising to 60%+ for Groom Club members.

facts.claim: At Urban Company, repeat customers acquired before FY23 contributed about 77% of FY23 Net Transaction Value, and the company expected this to exceed 90%. Spend per annual transacting consumer was Rs 3,786 (FY23), Rs 3,959 (FY24) and Rs 4,079 (FY25).

facts.notes: Primary company disclosure (FY23). The spend-per-consumer series comes from secondary IPO summaries (e.g., https://www.tradejini.com/blogs/urban-company-ipo-overview). Shows that a mature home-services marketplace depends on repeat GMV.
